newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI ups loan share in working capital credit.
newsitem.headline: India RBI ups loan share in working capital credit.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Saturday the loan component of working capital credit disbursed by banks would be enhanced.

In its monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March), the RBI said the loan component was being enhanced while the cash credit component was being scaled down to impart discipline in the utilisation of bank credit.
Working capital loans in India are a mix of cash credit and fixed instalment loan facilities.
The loan component stood enhanced to 75 percent from 60 percent for loans of 200 million rupees and above, the RBI said.
The loan component for borrowers with loans of 100 million rupees and above but less than 200 million was increased to 60 percent from the existing 40 percent, the RBI said.
Other related changes announced by the RBI include a decrease in the minimum loan period to six months from one year. The loan component could be rolled over or renewed, the RBI added.
Borrowers could hereafter include their borrowings under bills in the loan component while at present they do so from the cash credit limits, the RBI said.
